name: Disclosure
oneline: Makes it clear where AI is involved — an AI action, an agent at work, or content AI produced — at the point it matters.

states.label: Resting
states.trigger: Nothing has been chosen for AI to act on yet.
states.behaviour: The AI action control: the AI action mark and its verb. Nothing is labelled — AI has not done anything yet.
states.meaning: Nothing here came from AI. The one control that would use it is recognisable.
states.action: Press Rewrite to choose what it applies to.

states.label: AI action available
states.trigger: Something is selected, so Rewrite now applies to it.
states.behaviour: Rewrite becomes available and says, in words, what it will do and that nothing is replaced until they review it.
states.meaning: Pressing Rewrite asks AI to change the selection — before anything has happened.
states.action: Press Rewrite, or keep editing by hand.

states.label: AI working
states.behaviour: The action mark becomes the working mark and the button reads “Rewriting…”. Progress and Stop sit with it, and a screen reader hears “Agent working”. Nothing changes until the result arrives.
states.meaning: The agent is doing it now. This is not the result yet.

states.label: AI-generated content
states.behaviour: The “Generated with AI” label, attached to the content it describes, with Undo.
states.meaning: This content was written by AI — and it has not been checked.
states.action: Open the label for details, keep editing, or Undo.

states.label: Additional details
states.behaviour: The label opens a panel in place: what Aria did, what it used, what it did not check, and that the original is kept. No model names or pipeline detail.
states.meaning: What the agent did, in terms they can judge without technical knowledge.
states.action: Show the original, close the details, or Undo.

simNote: A release note three people wrote. Ask Aria to rewrite your paragraph and watch the three meanings stay apart: the action says what it will do, the working state says it is doing it, and the result says it came from AI — then open the document as the reviewer and check the label is still there.
intent: Answers “where is AI involved here?” at the moment it matters: the action that will use AI says so before it runs, the agent’s work is visibly in progress, and what it produced is labelled where it sits — so people can judge it.
when: Wherever AI acts on something a person owns or will rely on: a rewrite in an editor, a drafted reply, a generated summary, a filled field. Mark the action before it runs, the work while it runs, and the result for as long as it is on the page — including for the colleague who opens it later.

name: Consent
oneline: Asks before the agent accesses something sensitive or takes an important action — what, why, the scope, and two real choices.

states.label: Consent required
states.trigger: The agent reached something it may not do without permission.
states.behaviour: Work pauses at that step. The request names what is asked, why this task needs it, the scope, and what happens next — with two choices of equal size. Nothing is preselected.
states.meaning: Nothing has been accessed or done. It is waiting for them.
states.action: Continue, Not now, or review the details first.

states.label: Reviewing access
states.behaviour: The request opens in place: the account, where activity is shown, and how to turn it off later. The choices stay where they were.
states.meaning: Exactly what they are agreeing to, before they agree.

states.label: Approved
states.behaviour: A short confirmation replaces the request: what was allowed, for how long, and where to take it back. The task continues.
states.meaning: Permission was given — only what was shown.
states.action: Carry on, review it, or turn it off.

states.label: Denied
states.behaviour: Nothing is accessed or done. Their request and the conversation are kept, and the product offers another way to continue.
states.meaning: No was a real answer, and the rest of the product still works.
states.action: Continue without it, use another source, or allow it after all.

states.label: Expired
states.trigger: Permission given earlier no longer applies.
states.behaviour: The request comes back with the reason it is being asked again — time, or what changed — rather than as if it were the first time.
states.meaning: Why they are being asked again, so the repeat is not noise.

states.label: Revoked
states.behaviour: Access stops at once. What was already read or done is stated plainly; nothing new happens until they allow it again.
states.meaning: They are back in control, and they can see where things stand.
states.action: Allow again later, if they want to.
states.next: Consent required, the next time it is needed

simNote: The request is ordinary; the permission is a consequence of it. Send it, and the agent stops at the one step it is not allowed to take. Continue and Not now both lead somewhere useful.
intent: Answers “do I want to allow the agent to do this?” at the moment access or an action is needed — with what is asked, why this task needs it, exactly what it covers, and two real choices. Nothing happens before the answer, and no answer costs the person their work.
when: Before the agent reads data it was not given, before an action others will see or that is hard to undo, and before a permission outlives the conversation. Ask again only when something changed — it expired, or the thing being approved is different — and say why.

name: Caveat
oneline: Says what is incomplete, uncertain or out of date about this result — attached to it, with a next step.

states.label: No caveat needed
states.trigger: Every source was read and nothing about the result is in doubt.
states.behaviour: The result on its own. No empty notice, no standing “AI can make mistakes” line.
states.meaning: There is nothing specific to be careful about.

states.label: Caveat visible
states.trigger: Two of the eight interviews could not be opened.
states.behaviour: One note at the foot of the summary it qualifies: what is missing, why it matters, and what to do. Calm tokens, not the error colour. The summary stays — nothing was removed because it is incomplete.
states.meaning: This summary reflects 6 of 8 interviews and may miss something.
states.action: Review sources, or reconnect the missing ones.

states.label: Details expanded
states.behaviour: The note opens in place to list what was read and what was not, each with its reason.
states.meaning: Exactly which inputs are behind the result, and which are not.

states.label: User resolves the issue
states.trigger: They reconnected the folder and Aria re-read the missing interviews.
states.behaviour: The note becomes a short confirmation of what changed — all 8 read, one theme added — and the new line is marked in the summary.
states.meaning: The gap is closed, and they can see what it changed.
states.action: Read the update, then dismiss it.

states.label: Caveat no longer relevant
states.trigger: The reason for the caveat is gone.
states.behaviour: The caveat leaves with its reason. The summary stands on its own, now from all eight.
states.meaning: Nothing about this result needs special care any more.

simNote: Limitation → explanation → recovery → resolution. Ask for the summary; two interviews will not open, and the caveat says exactly that — then reconnect them and watch it go. Compare it with the generic line.
intent: Answers “what should I be careful about with this result?” — specifically, attached to the result it qualifies, with why it matters and what to do next. It appears only when there is a real limitation and leaves when the reason for it is gone.
when: When something about this result is meaningfully incomplete, uncertain, out of date or limited, and that changes how far it can be relied on. Not on results the product can stand behind, and never as a standing disclaimer.

name: Avatar
oneline: One mark for the agent on every surface — never mistakable for a person, with its working state on the mark itself.

states.label: Resting
states.trigger: The agent is present and idle.
states.behaviour: The agent avatar (rounded square, agent role), its name and “AI agent”. No ring, no motion.
states.meaning: The agent is here and available.

states.label: Active
states.trigger: The agent is engaged — listening, or assigned.
states.behaviour: A still outline ring in md-primary around the same avatar, and the words “Active now”.
states.meaning: The agent is engaged right now.

states.label: Working
states.behaviour: Md3CircularProgress turns around the same avatar, with “Working…” beside it. The mark itself does not change.
states.meaning: The agent is working now.

states.label: Compact
states.trigger: Space is tight: a list row, a chip, a notification.
states.behaviour: The same mark at 24 — same shape, same container — with the name beside it.
states.meaning: The same agent, in less space.

states.label: Fallback
states.trigger: The approved image did not load.
states.behaviour: The package fallback: the agent glyph on muted (or initials on brand). Shape and accessible label stay.
states.meaning: Still the agent — only the picture is missing.

simNote: A meeting with two people and an agent. Ask Aria for a summary and watch its mark: it rings while it works, and it never looks like Maya or Jordan. Then break the image, or draw Aria like a person, and compare.
intent: Answers “is that the agent, and is it doing something?” at a glance — in a meeting, a message, a list or a chip — without relying on colour, motion or a face.
when: Anywhere the agent appears or acts next to people: meeting participants, messages, notifications, activity, mentions and the composer chip that addresses it.

name: Name
oneline: A short, consistent name and role for the agent — the same on every surface, never a real person’s name.

states.label: Introduced
states.trigger: The agent appears for the first time.
states.behaviour: Avatar, name, role and “AI agent”, then one sentence: who runs it, what it does, and that it is not a person.
states.meaning: This is Aria, an AI agent, and this is what it is for.

states.label: Standard
states.trigger: Anywhere the agent is named with room to spare.
states.behaviour: The avatar with the name and the role beside it, in the same words as the introduction.
states.meaning: This is Aria.

states.label: Compact
states.trigger: A chip, a notification, an activity line.
states.behaviour: The name alone (or name · role) at 24 with the mark. The accessible name still includes the role.
states.meaning: The same agent, briefly.

states.label: Multiple agents
states.trigger: More than one agent in the same product.
states.behaviour: Each has its own name, role and glyph, so they are told apart by more than colour.
states.meaning: Which agent is which.

states.label: Name updated
states.behaviour: The new name with “formerly Aria” beside it, and an Md3Snackbar saying the role and permissions did not change — with Undo.
states.meaning: Same agent, new name. Nothing else changed.

simNote: The same agent in the chat, the activity log and the email it sends. Ask a question, then rename it as an admin — or switch on inconsistent naming and see three products where there is one agent.
intent: Answers “who am I talking to, and what is it for?” — with a name people can say and refer to, a role that says what it does, and an introduction that says it is AI and who runs it.
when: Whenever the agent is a participant people address or refer to — not for a single feature button.

name: Personality
oneline: Lets people choose how the agent writes — with a preview — while permissions, facts and safety language stay exactly the same.

states.label: Default
states.behaviour: The recommended option, Calm & precise, selected. Each option says how it writes; one line says permissions, facts and safety stay the same.
states.meaning: This changes how the agent writes — nothing else.

states.label: Preview
states.behaviour: A sample reply in Warm. Nothing is applied until Apply.
states.meaning: This is what Warm would sound like.

states.label: Applied
states.behaviour: Warm is selected and an Md3Snackbar confirms it, with Undo.
states.meaning: The agent writes warmly from now on.

states.label: Changed
states.trigger: They are back in the conversation.
states.behaviour: One quiet notice — “Personality changed to Warm. Facts, permissions and safety are unchanged.” — with Reset.
states.meaning: The style changed; the rules did not.

states.label: Reset
states.behaviour: Calm & precise is selected again, with a snackbar that says so.
states.meaning: Back to the recommended style.

simNote: Switch Aria between three personalities and read the same conversation each time. The reply changes; the permission request and the caveat do not. Then let a playful personality override them, and see what breaks.
intent: Answers “how will this sound, and what will it not change?” — a small set of writing styles, previewed on the same messages before applying, with the trust language fixed in every one.
when: When people spend long stretches with the agent and its default voice may not suit them. Not as a persona or a character that claims to be a person, and not in regulated output where tone reads as opinion.

name: Iconography
oneline: One Material Symbol per AI meaning — action, working, tool use, generated — always with words, never one sparkle for everything.

states.label: Resting
states.behaviour: The role glyph and its verb. Nothing glows or moves.
states.meaning: Pressing this runs AI on something specific.

states.label: Hover
states.behaviour: The Md3 state layer at 8% and the Md3Tooltip: what will happen, in words.
states.meaning: What the control will do.

states.label: Focus
states.behaviour: The focus ring (md-primary) and the same tooltip.
states.meaning: The same, without a pointer.

states.label: Pressed
states.behaviour: The 12% state layer. The glyph does not change yet.
states.meaning: Your press was received.

states.label: Working
states.behaviour: The action glyph becomes the working glyph (progress_activity) and the label becomes “Rewriting…”.
states.meaning: The agent is doing it now.

states.label: Disabled
states.trigger: There is nothing to act on.
states.behaviour: The control at 38% with its reason as supporting text — never an unexplained grey icon.
states.meaning: Why it is unavailable, and what to do.

simNote: A support reply. Press Rewrite and watch four different marks appear for four different meanings — action, working, tool use, generated. Then switch on “one sparkle for everything” and try to tell them apart.
intent: Answers “what does this AI mark mean here?” — will run AI, is running, used a tool, or was written by AI — consistently across the product, with a label or tooltip so the icon is never the only explanation.
when: On controls that run AI, on the working state, on tool-use steps and on AI-generated content. Not on features without AI, and not as decoration, branding or “premium”.

name: Color
oneline: Semantic colour roles from Nucleux tokens for the agent, attention, evidence and status — always paired with an icon and words.

states.label: Default
states.behaviour: A neutral surface with an outline, the agent glyph and “Available”.
states.meaning: Nothing needs attention.

states.label: Active
states.trigger: The task is assigned to the agent.
states.behaviour: The agent role (md-primary-container), the agent glyph and “Assigned to Aria”.
states.meaning: The agent owns this.

states.label: Working
states.behaviour: The agent role, the working glyph and what it is doing.
states.meaning: The agent is working now.

states.label: Attention
states.behaviour: The attention role (md-tertiary-container), a help glyph and “Needs your approval”.
states.meaning: You need to decide something.

states.label: Success
states.behaviour: A check glyph in the success colour on a neutral surface, so the text keeps its contrast, and “Complete”.
states.meaning: Done.

states.label: Warning
states.behaviour: The warning role with its foreground, a warning glyph and the specific reason.
states.meaning: Look at this soon.

states.label: Error
states.behaviour: The error role (md-error-container), an error glyph and what failed. Never used for anything else.
states.meaning: It failed.

simNote: A launch board. Assign the checklist to Aria and follow it from available to working, approval, source used and done — every state a token role with its own glyph and words. Turn on greyscale: nothing is lost. Turn on colour only: everything is.
intent: Answers “what needs me, what is the agent doing, and what went wrong?” with colour that means something — agent, attention, evidence, success, warning, error — and that still reads in greyscale, dark theme and to a screen reader.
when: For the agent’s presence and work, for states that need a decision, for sources it used, and for outcomes. Not for decoration, gradients or glows, and never by remapping error or warning to brand colours.

name: Example Gallery
oneline: A small set of real, product-specific tasks the agent does well — choosing one places an editable request in the composer.

states.label: Examples available
states.trigger: The person has not started yet.
states.behaviour: A few real tasks, grouped by kind, each with one line on what it does and what it needs. The composer is right below for their own words.
states.meaning: This is the kind of thing the agent is good at.

states.label: Example selected
states.behaviour: The example opens to show the exact request it will place, and what it uses. Nothing is filled yet.
states.meaning: What choosing this would do.

states.label: Placed into workflow
states.behaviour: The request is in the composer, editable and unsent. The example is marked “In composer”.
states.meaning: It is their request now.
states.action: Edit it, send it, or clear it.

states.label: Example edited
states.behaviour: Their version is what will be sent. The example no longer claims it.
states.meaning: The example was a starting point.

states.label: Active interaction
states.behaviour: The agent is working. The gallery steps back to a “Show examples” button (or a row of chips), so the work is the focus.
states.meaning: Normal work has started.
states.action: Wait, stop, or show examples again.

simNote: A new conversation in a meeting workspace. Pick an example — it lands in the composer, unsent. Edit it (type, or use “Edit the request”), send it, and watch the gallery step back.
intent: Answers “what can I do with this agent?” with a few real tasks from this product — grouped, each saying what it uses — so people start from something that works instead of guessing what to ask.
when: On an empty or new conversation, and on demand afterwards. Not as a standing panel that competes with the work once it has started.

name: Templates
oneline: A reusable setup for a repeatable workflow — previewed first, applied as editable fields, never run on its own.

states.label: Template available
states.trigger: The person is starting a recurring piece of work.
states.behaviour: A short list of workflow templates, each saying what it produces and what it uses.
states.meaning: There is a ready-made setup for this.

states.label: Preview
states.behaviour: What it asks for, what it produces, the tools it uses and anything it needs — before anything is applied.
states.meaning: Exactly what this template will set up.

states.label: Applied
states.behaviour: The fields are in place and editable. A value Aria suggested is marked until they keep or change it. Nothing has run.
states.meaning: The setup is ready; they decide what goes in it.

states.label: Edited
states.behaviour: Their values are confirmed; Run becomes available once required fields are filled. Replacing the template asks first.
states.meaning: It is their request now.

states.label: Missing requirement
states.trigger: The template needs Google Drive, and it isn’t connected.
states.behaviour: What is missing, why it is needed and what they can do — Connect Drive or Use without Drive. Their values stay.
states.meaning: One thing is needed before it can do all of this.

states.label: Removed / reset
states.behaviour: The template is gone and what was there before is back, with Undo.
states.meaning: Nothing was lost.

simNote: A research workspace. Preview the Competitive analysis template, apply it, and hit the one thing it needs — web access. Turn it on and see your values still there. Nothing runs until you press Run.
intent: Answers “how do I start this workflow I do every week?” with a structure they can see before applying: what it asks for, what it produces, what it uses — and what it needs that isn’t connected yet.
when: For workflows people repeat with the same shape — weekly updates, analyses, reviews. Not for one-off prompts (use Suggested Prompts or Example Gallery).

name: Nudges
oneline: A quiet, dismissible tip about a capability that would help right now — with a reason, and it doesn’t come back once dismissed.

states.label: Dormant
states.trigger: Nothing about what they are doing makes a capability useful right now.
states.behaviour: Nothing is shown.

states.label: Nudge shown
states.trigger: They selected transcript text again — something Aria can work with.
states.behaviour: One line in the flow: what they can do, why it appeared (on request), Try it, Not now and Dismiss. It never blocks the work.
states.meaning: There is a capability that would help with what they are doing.
states.action: Try it, not now, dismiss — or ignore it.
states.next: Accepted, Dismissed, Snoozed or No longer relevant

states.label: Accepted
states.behaviour: The nudge leaves and the capability opens where they are working. It will not promote this again.
states.meaning: They know about it now.

states.label: Dismissed
states.behaviour: The nudge leaves, with an Undo. It does not come back for this capability.
states.meaning: Their choice is remembered.

states.label: Snoozed
states.behaviour: The nudge leaves for a week, with an Undo.
states.meaning: It may come back later — not today.

states.label: No longer relevant
states.behaviour: The nudge withdraws on its own, quietly — the reason for it is gone.

simNote: Reviewing a transcript by hand. Select a second passage and a quiet tip appears — not a dialog. Try it and the selection goes into the composer as context; dismiss it and it stays gone.
intent: Answers “is there something here I might have missed?” at the moment it is useful, without interrupting: one line in the flow, why it appeared, and an easy way to try it, snooze it or dismiss it.
when: When the person is doing something a capability would make easier — and only once. Not on page load, not as an advert, and not again after it was used or dismissed.

name: Disclaimer / Agent Limits
oneline: States what the agent can’t reliably do — briefly in general, specifically where it matters, and with a way forward when it hits a limit.

states.label: General limits available
states.trigger: Where the agent is introduced, or from its menu.
states.behaviour: One or two sentences on the limits that matter most, with “See what Aria can and can’t do”.
states.meaning: The boundaries worth knowing before relying on it.

states.label: Details expanded
states.behaviour: Four short groups: what it can do, can’t do, needs approval for, and may get wrong — and where to review.
states.meaning: When to rely on it, and when to check or take over.

states.label: Contextual limit shown
states.trigger: They are about to ask for something that needs Jira.
states.behaviour: The relevant limit, at the point it matters, with what they can do instead.
states.meaning: Before asking: this part needs Jira.
states.action: Connect Jira, or continue without creating tasks.

states.label: Limit encountered
states.trigger: Aria reached the boundary during the task.
states.behaviour: An Md3Banner says what happened, that their work is kept, and the next steps. Not the error colour.
states.meaning: It stopped at a limit — nothing was lost.
states.action: Connect Jira, or review the drafts.

states.label: Recovery / next step
states.behaviour: They continue with the drafts. The limit stays one line away, with Connect Jira when they are ready.
states.meaning: The work carries on without the missing part.

simNote: Ask Aria to create Jira tasks from a meeting. The general limits are one line at the top; the specific one appears when the request needs it, and again when Aria reaches it — with your drafts kept and two ways on.
intent: Answers “what can’t this agent do, and when should I check its work?” in plain words: a short general statement, the specific limit at the point it applies, and — when the agent reaches it — what happened, that the work is kept, and what to do next.
when: Where the agent is introduced (general), before an action it can’t complete (contextual), and when it reaches a boundary during a task. Not as a standing warning on every message.

name: Initial CTA
oneline: The large, inviting input that anchors the empty state.

states.label: Resting
states.trigger: The workspace has no conversation, task or history yet.
states.behaviour: The large composer is the focal point, with its placeholder suggesting what to do. Send is unavailable because there is nothing to send. Secondary actions stay quiet around it.
states.action: Click or tab into the field.

states.label: Focused
states.trigger: The field receives focus — a click, a tap, or Tab.
states.behaviour: The outline takes the primary colour and the corner squares up a step. The placeholder stays until the first keystroke and the send key is named underneath. The layout does not move.

states.label: Typing
states.behaviour: The placeholder is gone and the field grows line by line up to its ceiling. Send is available at a secondary emphasis while keys are moving; nothing else competes with the text.

states.label: Ready to submit
states.trigger: A request is in the field and the person has paused.
states.behaviour: Send takes the primary fill. The request is still fully editable, and nothing is sent until the person sends it.
states.action: Send it — Enter, or the send button.

states.label: Active conversation
states.behaviour: The request enters the workspace as the first turn, the agent starts, and the SAME composer shrinks and moves to its working place at the bottom. From here on it is the normal composer.
states.action: Keep going in the working composer, or pick Resting to start over.

simNote: An empty planning workspace. The large composer is the only thing to do here — type a request and send it, and watch the same composer move into its working place.
intent: Answer "where do I start?" with a field, not a button — and let that field become the working composer the moment work begins.
when: Whenever the main agent workspace has no conversation, task or history to show — a new conversation, a fresh project, a cleared thread. For people who already know agentic products as much as for anyone: this is not a tutorial, it is the empty state of the work surface.
whenNot: Once there is meaningful activity. Leaving the oversized input in place beside a conversation turns an invitation into furniture competing with the work. Not as a marketing CTA, a sign-up prompt or a first-run explainer, and not as a replacement for Suggested Prompts — those are separate patterns and they stay visually secondary if they appear at all.

name: Open Input
oneline: Free-form text box for any natural-language ask.

states.label: Empty
states.trigger: The conversation is running and nothing is typed.
states.behaviour: The working composer at its compact size, docked under the conversation, placeholder showing. Send is unavailable. Not an invitation — the conversation is the focus.
states.action: Click or tab into the field. Next: Focused.

states.label: Focused
states.behaviour: Primary outline, the corner squares up a step, the caret is there. The placeholder stays until the first keystroke. Nothing moves.

states.label: Typing
states.behaviour: The placeholder goes and the text is the focus. Send is available at a secondary emphasis while keys are moving; the other controls still work and leave the text alone.
states.action: Keep typing or edit. Next: Multi-line, or Ready to send.

states.label: Multi-line
states.trigger: The request wraps, or Shift + Enter adds a line.
states.behaviour: The composer eases taller a line at a time, controls anchored to the bottom row, up to its maximum — then the field scrolls inside itself.
states.action: Continue typing, edit, or send. Next: Ready to send, or Empty.

states.label: Ready to send
states.trigger: Valid content is in the field and the person has paused.
states.behaviour: Send takes the primary fill. The request is still fully editable; nothing sends until the host’s send key or the button.
states.action: Send. Next: Submitted — or Error, if it fails.

states.label: Submitted
states.behaviour: The request is the newest turn; only now is the field cleared. The composer stays where it is, empty and focused. While Aria answers, Send is Stop and the field is still live.
states.action: Write the next request. Next: Focused, Typing.

states.label: Error / unavailable
states.trigger: The send did not go through.
states.behaviour: One sentence in human words, inside the composer, with Retry. The request is exactly as it was and still editable. No code, no cleared field.
states.action: Edit, then Retry or send. Next: Submitted.

simNote: A conversation already under way, with the working composer where it always is. Type a follow-up, change the model or add context mid-sentence, send it — and try a failed send: the text stays.
intent: The default way to talk to the agent once work is under way — free-form, always there, and never careless with what someone has typed.
when: Wherever a person can make a request in words during ongoing work — conversational agents, task and coding agents, research tools, support agents, project workspaces, side panels — as the default entry point after the first request. Before any activity, the same composer is drawn at its larger Initial CTA size.
whenNot: Not as the empty-state invitation (that is Initial CTA, the same composer at another size), not as a structured form when the request genuinely has fixed fields, and not as a command-only or search-only box. If the set of things a person can ask for is small and known, buttons beat a blank field.

name: Suggested Prompts
oneline: Smart, context-aware preset actions to jumpstart engagement.

states.label: Suggestions available
states.trigger: The workspace has context worth asking about and nothing is typed.
states.behaviour: Three suggestions just below the composer, each an action named from what is on screen. The composer is level one and works on its own; the set is level two.
states.action: Choose one, or ignore them and type. Next: Suggestion selected — or Prompt edited.

states.label: Suggestion selected
states.trigger: The person activates a suggestion (click, tap, Enter or Space).
states.behaviour: The suggestion takes the secondary-container fill and its text travels into the composer. Nothing is sent. Focus moves to the field, and the placement is announced.
states.action: Let it land. Next: Prompt placed in composer.

states.label: Prompt placed in composer
states.trigger: The chosen prompt has landed in the field.
states.behaviour: Ordinary composer text with the caret at the end — not a chip, not locked. Send is ready. The set stays, the chosen one marked, so another can be chosen instead: it replaces the untouched text.
states.action: Edit, choose another, add context, change the model, or send. Next: Prompt edited, Suggestion selected, or the conversation.

states.label: Prompt edited
states.trigger: The person changes the placed text — or writes their own instead.
states.behaviour: It is simply their request now. No preset styling, no lock; the set steps aside, so no suggestion can overwrite their words. Clear the field and the suggestions come back.

states.label: Conversation started
states.behaviour: The request is the first turn and Aria answers. The suggestions do not come back: they are an entry aid, not navigation. The composer stays, empty and ready.
states.action: Continue in the composer. Reset from the state list.

simNote: A planning workspace with the September release open. Three suggestions sit above the composer, each drawn from what the workspace shows. Choose one, change it, send it — or switch workspace in the sidebar and watch the suggestions follow.
intent: Answer "what should I ask?" with three or four real actions from this workspace — and hand the chosen one to the composer as the person's own, editable text.
when: On an empty or new conversation in a workspace with visible context worth asking about — a release plan, a research study, a design file, a ticket, a document — and in side panels opened next to that context. Wherever people hesitate over the first request.
whenNot: Not as autocomplete (that completes what someone is already typing), not as proactive suggestions (the agent raising a next step because of something that happened), not as templates (structured scaffolds with fields), and not as a prompt library, marketplace or command menu. Not throughout a conversation: once it has started, the suggestions have done their job.

name: Icons
oneline: One stable mark per AI meaning: action, generated content, agent working, tool use.

states.label: Resting
states.trigger: The editor is open with a draft in it.
states.behaviour: Rewrite carries the AI-action mark beside its word; Link and Attach carry ordinary icons.
states.meaning: “AI will do something specific when I press this.”
states.action: Point at, tab to, or press Rewrite. Clear the draft to see Disabled.

states.label: Hover
states.behaviour: The 8% Material state layer, and the tooltip “Rewrite with AI”.
states.meaning: The same AI action, offered.

states.label: Focus
states.behaviour: The visible focus ring and the 12% layer; the tooltip shows on focus too, and Escape hides it.
states.meaning: The same AI action, ready for Enter or Space.
states.action: Enter or Space presses it; Tab moves on.

states.label: Pressed
states.behaviour: The 12% pressed layer. Releasing it starts the work.
states.meaning: “I asked AI to do this.”

states.label: Working
states.behaviour: The button’s mark changes from the AI-action mark to the turning working mark, and its word to “Rewriting…”. It is unavailable until the work ends; the draft stays readable.
states.meaning: The requested AI operation is running now.
states.action: Wait, or Stop where the product supports cancelling.

states.label: Complete
states.behaviour: Rewrite returns to its AI-action mark, and a short line confirms the result with Undo.
states.meaning: The AI action is done, and can be run again.
states.action: Keep it, Undo, or press Rewrite again.

states.label: Disabled
states.trigger: There is nothing for the AI to act on — the draft is empty.
states.behaviour: Rewrite dims to 38% but keeps its AI-action mark and stays focusable; its tooltip says why: “Write something first”.
states.meaning: This is still an AI action, unavailable for now.

states.label: Disclosed
states.trigger: The release note holds text Aria wrote.
states.behaviour: One “Generated with AI” label, with the generated-content mark, sits under the text it describes — once, not on every line.
states.meaning: “This content came from AI.” Disclosure, not an action.
states.action: Point at or tab to the label; press it for details.

states.label: Hover or focus
states.trigger: A pointer rests on the label, or it receives keyboard focus.
states.behaviour: The state layer, the focus ring on focus, and a tooltip saying who wrote it and from what.
states.meaning: The same provenance, explained in a sentence.
states.action: Press for details, or move on.

states.label: Details
states.behaviour: A rich tooltip says what Aria did and from what, and offers the original back.
states.meaning: What AI changed, and how to reverse it.

states.label: Working
states.trigger: An AI action started — here, Rewrite.
states.behaviour: The working mark turns steadily beside “Rewriting release note…”, with Stop. Screen readers hear “Agent working: rewriting release note”, not the animation.
states.meaning: The agent is doing something right now.

states.label: Complete
states.behaviour: The turning mark is gone the moment the work ends; a still line says what was done.
states.meaning: Nothing is running any more.
states.action: Read the result, or run it again.

states.label: Stopped
states.trigger: Stop was pressed while the agent worked.
states.behaviour: The mark stops and goes; the line says the draft is unchanged.
states.meaning: The work was cancelled; nothing changed.
states.action: Run it again, or carry on.

states.label: Tool used
states.trigger: Aria checked the draft against the team’s style guide before suggesting changes.
states.behaviour: An activity line led by the tool-use mark names the tool and the act: “Style guide checked”.
states.meaning: “The agent used another capability to do this work.”
states.action: Point at or tab to it; press it for what was checked.

states.label: Hover or focus
states.trigger: A pointer rests on the activity line, or it receives keyboard focus.
states.behaviour: The state layer, the focus ring on focus, and a tooltip naming the system.
states.meaning: The same tool use, named in full.

states.label: Details
states.behaviour: It expands in place to list what the tool found and what changed because of it.
states.meaning: What the tool contributed, inspectable.

simNote: One AI interaction, four meanings. Press Rewrite and watch each stage keep its own mark: the action, the work, the tool and the result never borrow each other’s.
intent: Give each AI meaning its own mark — run AI, made by AI, the agent is working, the agent used a tool — and keep each mark for that meaning only, everywhere in the product.
when: Wherever a product mixes AI capability with ordinary controls and content: toolbars and menus with AI actions, fields the agent can fill, documents and records holding AI-written text, and any surface where the agent works in the background or reaches into other systems.
whenNot: Not for "new", "premium" or "beta" — those get words. Not as decoration on a feature that happens to be recent. Not as the agent's identity (that is the avatar and name), and not as a substitute for a label where a mistaken press matters.

name: Autocomplete
oneline: Ghost text that anticipates and completes user actions.

states.label: Empty / no suggestion
states.behaviour: The composer as usual. Nothing is suggested before the person starts — that would be Suggested Prompts, not autocomplete.

states.label: Typing
states.trigger: Text is entered, but not enough to finish usefully — or nothing matches.
states.behaviour: No suggestion. The composer behaves exactly as without autocomplete.

states.label: Suggestion available
states.trigger: What is typed is the start of a known request.
states.behaviour: The rest appears after the caret in a lighter colour with its key (Tab) at the end. It is not in the field: a screen reader hears “Suggestion: …”, separately from the text.
states.action: Tab (or tap it) to accept, Escape to dismiss, or keep typing. Next: Accepted, Ignored, Dismissed, No longer relevant.

states.label: Suggestion accepted
states.trigger: Tab, →, or a tap on the suggestion.
states.behaviour: It becomes ordinary editable text with the caret at the end. Nothing is sent; Send is ready for when the person is.
states.action: Edit it, or send. Next: Typing, or the conversation.

states.label: Suggestion ignored
states.trigger: The person keeps typing the same words instead of accepting.
states.behaviour: The suggestion follows along, shortening as they type — never overwriting a character they wrote.
states.action: Keep typing, or accept the rest. Next: Accepted, No longer relevant.

states.label: Suggestion dismissed
states.behaviour: It goes, and does not come back for this request while the person keeps writing the same words.

states.label: No longer relevant
states.trigger: What is typed stops matching the suggestion.
states.behaviour: It disappears at once. The person’s words are untouched.
states.action: Keep typing. Next: Typing, or a new suggestion.

simNote: Start a request in the composer. When what you type is the start of one people here often send, the rest appears after the caret. Tab takes it; it is never sent for you.
intent: Save typing on requests people make often, without taking any of the final instruction out of their hands.
when: In a composer or field where people repeat requests, refer to commands, people, files or tools by name, and where a completion can be predicted from what they have typed so far.
whenNot: Not before anything is typed (that is Suggested Prompts). Not for the agent raising something on its own (that is Proactive Suggestions). Not for structured scaffolds with fields (Templates). Not where a wrong completion is costly and hard to spot — legal, financial or medical wording.

name: Proactive Suggestions
oneline: Invisible AI moments that arrive exactly when needed.

states.label: Dormant
states.trigger: Nothing worth raising — or the reason has been dealt with.
states.behaviour: Nothing is shown. The agent watches the work, silently.
states.action: Simulate “Sam Ortiz moves to Payments”. Next: Suggested.

states.label: Suggested
states.trigger: The agent noticed something: two release blockers lost their owner.
states.behaviour: A compact card where the work is: who suggests it, why it appeared, what it recommends — as a question — and Review, Remind me tomorrow, Dismiss. Nothing has changed; the list is fully usable.
states.action: Review, snooze, dismiss — or fix it yourself. Next: Action preparing, Snoozed, Dismissed, No longer relevant.

states.label: Action preparing
states.behaviour: The working mark and “Preparing a review — nothing has changed yet.”

states.label: Accepted
states.behaviour: The proposed owners, each changeable, and one confirming action. Nothing is assigned until the person confirms.
states.action: Change, confirm (Undo stays available) or cancel. Next: Dormant.

states.label: Dismissed
states.behaviour: It goes, with Undo. It is remembered for these issues: the same evidence never brings it back — only something new does.
states.action: Carry on. Next: Dormant — or Suggested on new evidence.

states.label: Snoozed
states.trigger: The person chose Remind me tomorrow.
states.behaviour: It goes until tomorrow, 9:00, with Undo. It returns then only if the reason is still true.
states.action: Simulate “A day passes”. Next: Suggested, or Dormant if resolved.

states.label: No longer relevant
states.trigger: The reason stopped being true — the person assigned the owners themselves.
states.behaviour: It says so briefly and withdraws on its own.

simNote: Work through release readiness. When Aria notices something worth raising, it offers one next step — with the reason, and nothing done until you confirm.
intent: Surface an opportunity or a problem the person would otherwise have to go looking for, as a recommendation they can review, snooze or dismiss — never as an action already taken.
when: During ongoing work, when a specific, checkable condition becomes true and there is a clear next step: unowned blockers before a release, an unanswered email, a duplicate issue, a missed deadline, a step left out of a checklist.
whenNot: Not to start a conversation (that is Suggested Prompts) or to finish what someone is typing (Autocomplete). Not for low-value or speculative tips, not on a timer with no new evidence, and not as a modal that interrupts the task. Never as a disguised action: if it would change something, it is a review first.

name: Randomize
oneline: A 'dice' that kickstarts the experience with a fun result.

states.label: Ready
states.trigger: An exploratory workspace — campaign concepts for the Planboard 3.0 launch.
states.behaviour: One optional control above the composer, saying what it gives: a random starting direction. The composer works on its own.
states.action: Press Try a direction — or just type. Next: Generating.

states.label: Generating
states.trigger: Try a direction (or Generate another) was pressed.
states.behaviour: The working mark and “Finding a different direction…”. Nothing else changes.
states.action: Wait a moment. Next: New suggestion.

states.label: New suggestion
states.behaviour: One direction — a title and a line — marked as generated, with Use this and Generate another. Nothing is placed or run yet.
states.action: Use it, or generate another. Next: Applied, Generate another.

states.label: Generate another
states.behaviour: A different direction — never a repeat this round — with “2 of 2” and a way back to the previous one.
states.action: Keep going, step back, or use one. Next: Applied.

states.label: Replace confirmation
states.trigger: Use this, while the composer holds the person’s own words.
states.behaviour: It asks: replace the draft, add the direction below it, or cancel. Their words are never silently replaced.
states.action: Choose. Next: Applied, or back to the suggestion.

states.label: Applied to composer
states.behaviour: An editable prompt in the shared composer, focus and caret there. Nothing is sent.
states.action: Edit it, then send — or try another direction. Next: the conversation.

simNote: Exploring campaign directions for a launch. Try a direction for a random starting point, generate another until one is worth pursuing, then put it in the composer and make it yours.
intent: Help people explore alternatives — campaign angles, ideas, styles, presets — without inventing every one themselves, while the composer stays theirs.
when: Creative and exploratory work where variety is the point and nothing is at stake: campaign directions, naming, ideas, visual styles, presets, prompt inspiration, starting configurations for generative tools.
whenNot: Not in finance, legal, medical, safety, destructive or otherwise deterministic workflows, where a random "direction" has no value and may mislead. Not as a replacement for open input, and not as a disguised way to run something.

name: Voice Input
oneline: Speak into the composer; review the words, then send.

states.label: Ready
states.trigger: The composer at rest — here with a few words already typed.
states.behaviour: The ordinary composer with a microphone in it. No gradient, no capture.
states.meaning: You can type, or speak instead. Voice is optional.
states.action: Press the microphone (the first time, the browser asks for it).

states.label: Permission required
states.trigger: The microphone was pressed and access has not been given yet.
states.behaviour: A panel above the bar says what is needed, why, when it is on and how to stop. The composer stays usable under it.
states.meaning: Nothing is recording yet.
states.action: Allow microphone, or Not now (keep typing).

states.label: Listening
states.behaviour: The bar keeps its place and becomes the voice session: a lit microphone with a dot, “Listening · 0:04”, the words as they are heard after anything already typed, and Pause, Stop, Cancel. The gradient behind it swells a little with each word and settles in silence.
states.meaning: The microphone is on. Nothing is sent.
states.action: Pause, Stop (keep the words) or Cancel (discard this recording).

states.label: Paused
states.behaviour: The microphone turns off (“Paused · microphone off”), the dot goes, the gradient settles. What was heard stays.
states.meaning: Not listening; your progress is kept.

states.label: Processing
states.trigger: Stop was pressed, silence ended it, or the time limit was reached.
states.behaviour: The microphone is off. “Transcribing…”, with the gradient drifting slowly. Only Cancel is offered.
states.meaning: Turning speech into text. Still nothing sent.

states.label: Transcribed
states.behaviour: The bar is a text composer again. The words join what was typed, marked “From voice — check it before you send”, with Undo. The caret is in the field.
states.meaning: This is what was understood. It has not been sent.
states.action: Edit it, Undo it, or Send.

states.label: Editing transcript
states.trigger: The person changes the transcribed text.
states.behaviour: The marker reads “From voice · edited”; Undo still returns to what was typed before voice.
states.meaning: Your correction wins. Voice only drafted it.

states.label: Couldn’t understand
states.trigger: Too little could be made out to trust.
states.behaviour: A panel says what happened and keeps what was heard; the typed text is untouched. No guess is put in the field.
states.meaning: Nothing was lost, and nothing was guessed.
states.action: Retry, Edit captured text, or Type instead.

states.label: Unavailable
states.trigger: No microphone was found, or the device blocks it.
states.behaviour: The microphone button is unavailable with its reason; a note says so. Typing works exactly as before.
states.meaning: Voice is off for now; the composer is not.

simNote: Voice is a way of writing the request, not a different product. Speak, see exactly what was heard, fix it, and send it yourself.
intent: Speech as an INPUT method into the shared composer: speech → transcript → editable text → the person sends. Not a separate voice assistant.
when: Wherever a request is quicker said than typed, and the product already has a composer to say it into. Not as a novelty alternative to a keyboard that is there and working, and not at all where the request commits something that a misheard word would commit wrongly — there, hold the text for correction first.

name: Visual Input
oneline: Show an image, a photo or a window — as context you control.

states.label: No visual
states.trigger: The composer, with words typed and nothing shown yet.
states.behaviour: An ordinary composer. Visual context is offered under +.
states.meaning: Aria only has your words.
states.action: Press + to add an image, a photo, a screenshot or a window.

states.label: Selecting
states.behaviour: A menu lists only the sources this product allows: Upload image, Take photo, Choose a recent screenshot, Share screen.
states.meaning: Nothing is shared yet.
states.action: Choose a source, or close the menu.

states.label: Visual attached
states.behaviour: A card with a real preview joins the composer above the words, with its name, “Aria will see this when you send”, Replace and Remove. The words are untouched.
states.meaning: This is exactly what Aria will see — and only when you send.
states.action: Add words, Replace, Remove, or Send.

states.label: Sharing
states.trigger: A window was chosen to share.
states.behaviour: A persistent bar — red dot, “Sharing ‘Q3 metrics dashboard’”, Stop sharing — sits above the composer, and the card says it is live.
states.meaning: Aria can see this window, and only this window, until you stop.
states.action: Ask about it, or Stop sharing at any time.

states.label: Processing
states.trigger: The request was sent with a visual.
states.behaviour: The card says “Aria is reading this image…” with a slow sheen across the preview; Replace and Remove step aside.
states.meaning: Aria is using the visual now. Nothing else happens because of it.

states.label: Ready
states.behaviour: Your message shows the visual it carried; the answer says which visual it used. The composer is clear for the next request.
states.meaning: You can see what Aria used to answer.
states.action: Ask a follow-up, or add another visual.

states.label: Permission required
states.trigger: Take photo or Share screen was chosen.
states.behaviour: A panel above the composer says what is needed, why, when it is on and how to stop — and, for sharing, lets you choose the one window.
states.meaning: Nothing is captured or shared yet.
states.action: Choose the window (or Allow camera), or Cancel.
states.next: Sharing / Visual attached, or No visual.

states.label: Unsupported
states.trigger: A file that cannot be used was chosen (here, a video).
states.behaviour: A panel says what cannot be used and what can; the words stay.
states.meaning: Nothing was added.
states.action: Choose an image, or continue without it.

states.label: Failed
states.trigger: Aria could not read the image (too blurry).
states.behaviour: The card is marked, a panel says why, and the message is kept — nothing was sent without the image.
states.meaning: Nothing is lost; the request waits for you.
states.action: Retry, Replace, or Continue without it.

simNote: Show Aria what you are looking at, and stop showing it whenever you like. Sharing is a state you can always see, and stopping it never ends the conversation.
intent: Visual context joins the request in the shared composer: recognisable, removable, combined with words — and screen sharing is a visible, stoppable state.
when: Where the evidence is visual and describing it in words is slower or less accurate: error screens and stack traces, damage and defects, whiteboards, receipts, labels, charts in somebody else's document, field and medical photographs.

name: Handwriting Input
oneline: Write by hand; review what was recognized before it joins your message.

states.label: Ready
states.trigger: The pen in the composer was pressed.
states.behaviour: A writing pad opens above the composer, which stays where it was and keeps what was typed (“Next sprint:”). Undo, Clear and Close sit on the pad.
states.meaning: Nothing is written or recognized yet.
states.action: Write with a stylus, a finger or the mouse — or Close.

states.label: Writing
states.behaviour: Strokes appear as they are drawn. Undo removes the last stroke; Clear removes all of it. Recognize is offered; nothing is read yet.
states.meaning: This ink is the original. It is yours, not text yet.
states.action: Keep writing, Undo, Clear, or Recognize.

states.label: Recognizing
states.trigger: Recognize was pressed (or, in automatic mode, the pen paused).
states.behaviour: The status says “Recognizing your writing…”; a slow sheen crosses the ink, which stays in view. Undo and Clear step aside.
states.meaning: The ink is being read. Nothing joins the message because of it.

states.label: Recognized
states.behaviour: Under the ink: “Recognized: Review onboarding flaw?”. The uncertain word is a button marked “?”, and Add to message is disabled until it is settled.
states.meaning: This is what was read — not yet what you said.
states.action: Tap the uncertain word and choose, or Edit text.
states.next: Editing recognition, or Added to message.

states.label: Editing recognition
states.behaviour: The corrected word (“flow”) is marked as yours; nothing is uncertain any more, so Add to message is enabled.
states.meaning: The text reads right. It is still not in the message.
states.action: Add to message, or Edit text in the composer.

states.label: Added to message
states.behaviour: The words join what was typed — never replacing it — marked “From handwriting” with Undo. The ink is attached as “Handwritten note”, removable.
states.meaning: Accepted text. Nothing is sent until you send.
states.action: Edit, Undo, remove the original, or Send.
states.next: Ready (after sending), or back to what was typed (Undo).

states.label: Couldn’t recognize
states.trigger: Too little of the ink could be read to trust.
states.behaviour: A message says so; the ink stays on the pad. Rewrite, Retry, Keep original (send the ink as an image) and Switch to typing are offered. Nothing is guessed into the message.
states.meaning: Nothing is lost, and nothing was added.
states.action: Rewrite, Retry, Keep original, or Switch to typing.
states.next: Ready, Recognizing, or Added to message (original only).

states.label: Unavailable
states.trigger: The device has no pen or touch input (or handwriting is turned off).
states.behaviour: The pen is shown disabled; pressing it explains why, in a panel above the composer. The field works as always.
states.meaning: Handwriting is optional; typing never depends on it.

simNote: Handwriting is a way of writing the request, not a different product. Write, see what was recognized, settle anything uncertain, and add it to your message yourself.
intent: A pen in the shared composer. Handwriting, recognized text and accepted text stay distinct, and nothing uncertain is ever accepted silently.
when: On pen- and touch-capable surfaces, for short requests, notes and annotations where writing is quicker or more natural than typing. Not as the only way in: the field always works, and on a device without pen or touch the pen is shown unavailable and typing carries on.

name: Gesture Input
oneline: Circle or tap what's on screen; it joins your request by name.

states.label: Ready
states.trigger: A dashboard on screen and the composer below it.
states.behaviour: An ordinary composer with a Select on screen button.
states.meaning: Aria only has your words.

states.label: Selecting
states.behaviour: A toolbar on the dashboard — “Circle what you mean — or Tab to it” — with Circle, Highlight, Tap and Region, and Cancel. Every item on the dashboard becomes a button.
states.meaning: Nothing is selected or shared yet. A gesture here only points.
states.action: Circle, highlight, tap or drag a box — or Tab to an item and press Enter. Escape cancels.
states.next: Selection made, or Couldn’t identify selection.

states.label: Selection made
states.trigger: A gesture landed on one thing.
states.behaviour: That thing gets a boundary, and a bar on it names it — “Conversion chart” — with Adjust, Clear and Add to message.
states.meaning: This is what you pointed at. It is not in the message yet.
states.action: Add to message, Adjust, or Clear.

states.label: Context added
states.behaviour: A chip in the composer — “Selected: Conversion chart” — with ✕; the chart keeps a quiet “Selected” tag. The words are yours to write.
states.meaning: Aria will use the chart with your words, when you send.
states.action: Ask, remove the selection, or select something else.
states.next: Agent using selection, or Selection cleared.

states.label: Agent using selection
states.trigger: The message was sent with a selection.
states.behaviour: The chart says “Aria is looking at this” under a slow sheen; the chip is outlined. The answer names the chart it used.
states.meaning: Aria is using the chart — and only the chart. Nothing is changed.
states.next: Context added (the selection stays for follow-ups).

states.label: Selection cleared
states.behaviour: The chip and the boundary are gone; a note says Aria won’t use the chart, with Select something else.
states.meaning: The conversation continues without it.
states.action: Select something else, or keep typing.

states.label: Couldn’t identify selection
states.trigger: A gesture covered two things (or nothing).
states.behaviour: Both candidates are marked and a panel asks “Which did you mean?” with a button for each, Try again, Describe it instead and Clear. Nothing is guessed.
states.meaning: Nothing is selected until you say.
states.action: Choose one, try again, describe it in words, or clear.

simNote: Point at what you mean, and it joins your request by name. A gesture only points — it never changes anything — and when it could mean two things, Aria asks.
intent: Contextual screen selection on the shared composer: point at the thing, see it named, add it to the request — and an ambiguous selection asks rather than guesses.
when: Wherever a request is about something already on screen: a chart, a row, a region of a design, a paragraph. Not as the only way to refer to things — words always work — and never as a way to trigger actions.

name: Structured Input
oneline: A compact form for exact values — suggestions marked, actions confirmed.

states.label: Empty
states.trigger: Aria needs exact values and has none yet.
states.behaviour: A compact form under the request: Task, Owner, Due date, Priority — labels, helper text, required marks — and “Suggest values”.
states.meaning: Nothing will happen until the form is complete and you confirm.
states.action: Fill it in, or ask for suggestions.

states.label: Partially completed
states.behaviour: A count (“1 of 4 filled”); required fields still empty are marked by their label, not yet by an error.
states.meaning: You can carry on in any order.

states.label: Complete
states.trigger: Every required field has a value.
states.behaviour: Owner, Due date and Priority were filled in by Aria from the blocker — Aria’s message says so — and stay editable. A value you change is marked “Edited by you”. Review is ready.
states.meaning: Suggestions are offers. Nothing you set is changed for you.
states.next: Ready to submit, or Validation error.

states.label: Validation error
states.behaviour: The message sits under its field (“Pick a date after today”), the field is marked invalid, a summary counts what needs a look, and focus moves to the first one.
states.meaning: Nothing was sent. Your values are untouched.
states.action: Fix the field — the error clears as soon as it is right.

states.label: Ready to submit
states.behaviour: A summary of the values, which were suggested and which you edited, “What Aria will receive” (the exact payload), Back to edit and Create task.
states.meaning: Creating a task changes another system, so it waits for you.
states.action: Create task, or Back to edit.

states.label: Submitted
states.behaviour: “Task created — EXP-214”, the values, “What Aria received”, Undo and Open task.
states.meaning: The outcome is visible, and reversible.

states.label: Couldn’t submit
states.behaviour: An alert says what happened; every value is kept; Retry and Cancel.
states.meaning: Nothing was created, and nothing is lost.
states.next: Ready to submit / Submitted, or Complete.

simNote: Open input for the request, a small form for the exact values. Suggestions are offers you can see and change; creating the task waits for you.
intent: A small form that complements open input: the request starts in words; the exact values are set in fields, checked next to each field, reviewed, and only then acted on.
when: When an action needs specific, validated values (create a task, book a slot, file an expense), or when a request is ambiguous in ways a few fields settle faster than questions. Not for open questions, and not instead of the composer — the person can always say it in words.

name: Suggestions
oneline: Aria suggests one detail to add to the request you’re writing — marked as its suggestion, added only if you choose, never sent for you.

states.label: No suggestion
states.trigger: They are typing, or nothing would make the request better.
states.behaviour: The composer on its own. Nothing appears while keys are moving.
states.meaning: Carry on writing.

states.label: Suggestion available
states.trigger: They paused on “Summarize the September release.”
states.behaviour: A short row of suggestion chips just above the composer, marked as Aria’s: what each would add, why (on request), and Dismiss. Their text is untouched.
states.meaning: Aria thinks this would make the request better.
states.action: Add it, dismiss it, or keep typing.
states.next: Accepted, Dismissed or No longer relevant

states.label: Suggestion accepted
states.behaviour: The words are added after theirs — never replacing them — and a line names what was added, with Undo. Nothing is sent.
states.meaning: The request now includes it, and it is still theirs to edit.

states.label: Suggestion dismissed
states.behaviour: The suggestion goes and does not come back for this request.
states.meaning: Their request stays exactly as written.

states.label: No longer relevant
states.trigger: They rewrote the request so the suggestion no longer fits.
states.behaviour: The suggestion withdraws on its own, quietly.
states.meaning: Nothing to add right now.

simNote: Write the request — or press “Type the request” — and pause. Suggestions appear just above the composer. Add one, edit what you have, then send. Nothing is sent or rewritten for you.
intent: Helps someone improve a request they are already writing: after a pause, Aria offers a few relevant details — context, a constraint, an expected outcome — as chips they can add, ignore or dismiss. Their words are never replaced.
when: When a request in progress is missing a detail the product can reliably infer from context — a time range, an audience, a constraint. Not while someone is still typing, and not to propose a different request.

name: Madlibs
oneline: A request written as a sentence with a few labelled blanks — fill them, read the result, then edit it in the composer before sending.

states.label: Empty scaffold
states.trigger: A request that needs a few specific details.
states.behaviour: A sentence with labelled blanks. Required and optional blanks are marked; the assembled request shows what is still missing.
states.meaning: Fill these in and the request is written.

states.label: Partially completed
states.behaviour: Filled blanks read as part of the sentence; the rest are still marked.
states.meaning: What is done, and what is left.

states.label: AI suggestion available
states.trigger: Aria can infer a value from what they chose.
states.behaviour: The blank shows Aria’s value, marked “Suggested”, with Keep and Clear. It is not part of the request until kept.
states.meaning: A likely value — theirs to accept.

states.label: Complete
states.trigger: Every required blank has a value they chose.
states.behaviour: The assembled sentence reads cleanly; Use prompt is available.
states.meaning: The request is written.

states.label: Validation needed
states.trigger: They pressed Use prompt with a required blank empty.
states.behaviour: That blank is flagged with words, focus moves to it, and everything else they entered stays.
states.meaning: One detail is missing.

states.label: Ready to use
states.behaviour: The sentence is in the composer — editable, unsent.
states.meaning: It is an ordinary request now.

simNote: Aria offers a guided sentence for a stakeholder summary. Fill the blanks — the request assembles as you go — then Use prompt puts it in the composer to edit and send.
intent: Helps someone write a request that needs a few specific details: a sentence with labelled blanks, required and optional marked, the assembled request visible as they go, and the result placed in the composer to edit — not sent.
when: For common requests with two to four variable details — summaries, briefs, comparisons. Not for open-ended requests, and not as a substitute for a form with many fields.

name: Prompt Enhancer
oneline: Proposes a clearer version of the request you wrote — every addition marked and explained, the original kept until you choose.

states.label: Original
states.trigger: They have written a short request.
states.behaviour: Their prompt in the composer, with Improve beside the model chip.
states.meaning: They can ask for a clearer version — or just send.

states.label: Enhancing
states.behaviour: Improve says “Improving…”; the original stays in the composer, readable and untouched.
states.meaning: Aria is working on a suggestion. Nothing has changed yet.

states.label: Enhanced
states.behaviour: A review above the composer: their words, plus each addition marked and explained. An assumption is labelled. The composer still holds the original.
states.meaning: What would change, and why.
states.action: Use it, edit it, remove a change, or keep the original.

states.label: Reviewing changes
states.behaviour: The removed addition is struck from the suggestion; the rest stay.
states.meaning: They are choosing which improvements to keep.
states.action: Use the rest, or restore it.

states.label: Edited
states.behaviour: The suggested prompt in a text field they can change freely.
states.meaning: The suggestion is a starting point.

states.label: Accepted
states.behaviour: The composer now holds the improved prompt — editable, unsent — with Undo.
states.meaning: Their request was updated; nothing was sent.

states.label: Reverted
states.behaviour: The original prompt is back exactly as written.
states.meaning: Nothing was lost.

states.label: Enhancement failed
states.behaviour: One line says so; the original is untouched. Try again, or keep the original.
states.meaning: Nothing changed.

simNote: Press Improve on a short request. Aria proposes a clearer one with every addition marked and explained — remove the one you don’t need, use the rest, and send. Your original stays until you choose.
intent: Helps someone improve a request they have already written: Aria proposes a clearer version, shows exactly what it added and why, flags assumptions, and leaves the original in the composer until they use, edit or reject the suggestion.
when: When a request is short or vague and the product can make it more specific without guessing the intent. Not for already-specific requests, and not to make every prompt longer.

name: Modes
oneline: Choose how the agent approaches the task — Brainstorm, Draft, Review, Plan — shown in the composer, separate from the model.

states.label: No mode selected
states.behaviour: A Mode control beside the model chip. Aria works the general way until a mode is chosen.
states.meaning: They can choose how Aria should approach this.

states.label: Mode picker open
states.behaviour: A short list of modes, each with one line on what changes. An unavailable mode says why.
states.meaning: What each mode would do with this request.

states.label: Mode selected
states.behaviour: The Mode chip in the composer now reads “Plan”, with a way to change or remove it. The text and the model are untouched.
states.meaning: Aria will approach this as a planning task.

states.label: Mode changed
states.behaviour: The chip updates and one line says what changed — and that their text is the same.
states.meaning: The next request will be a review.

states.label: Mode unavailable
states.trigger: They chose a mode this workspace can’t support.
states.behaviour: The mode isn’t applied; the picker says why and offers the others.
states.meaning: That approach isn’t possible here.

simNote: Open Mode in the composer and choose Plan, then send: Aria answers with steps. Switch to Review and ask again — same model, same context, a different way of working.
intent: Lets someone choose how the agent should work on a request — explore, draft, review, plan — without describing the working style every time. The mode is visible in the composer, changes nothing they wrote, and is separate from which model answers.
when: When the product genuinely works differently per approach — different steps, tools or output. Not as labels over the same behaviour, and not to stand in for model selection or reasoning effort.

name: Voice & Tone
oneline: Say how the reply should sound — Professional, Friendly, Concise, or your own words — visible in the composer, never changing what it says.

states.label: Default
states.behaviour: A Tone control beside the model chip. Aria uses its default voice.
states.meaning: They can say how the reply should sound.

states.label: Tone picker open
states.behaviour: Tones with one line each showing how it sounds; Aria’s recommendation is marked, not selected; a field for their own description.
states.meaning: How the reply would sound in each.
states.action: Choose one, describe one, or close.

states.label: Tone selected
states.behaviour: The Tone chip in the composer now reads “Professional”, with a way to change or remove it. Their text is untouched.
states.meaning: The reply will sound professional — saying the same things.

states.label: Custom tone
states.behaviour: Their words become the tone chip, with a note that Aria will match it as closely as it can.
states.meaning: Their description guides how it sounds.

states.label: Tone changed
states.behaviour: The chip updates; one line says the facts stay the same.
states.meaning: Same content, different voice.
states.action: Send, or ask for a new version.

states.label: Tone removed
states.behaviour: The chip goes; Aria uses its default voice. Undo is offered.
states.meaning: Back to the default.

simNote: Choose Professional and send. Then switch to Conversational and ask for another version — the wording changes, the facts don’t. Aria’s recommendation is marked and never applied for you.
intent: Lets someone set how a reply should sound for this audience — choosing a tone, or describing one — previewed in a line, visible in the composer, and changeable or removable before they send. Tone changes wording, never facts.
when: For writing tasks where the audience changes the voice — updates, replies, announcements. Not for analysis or factual lookups, and not as the agent’s standing personality (that is Personality).

name: Preset Styles
oneline: Named styles for how replies are written — Normal, Concise, Formal, Explanatory, or one made from your own writing — previewed, switchable mid-conversation.

states.label: Normal
states.behaviour: No style chip: Aria writes the way it usually does. A Style control sits with the composer’s tools.
states.meaning: Replies use the default style.

states.label: Style menu open
states.behaviour: “Use style”: Normal, Concise, Formal and Explanatory, each with one line on what changes, their own styles below, and Create & edit styles. The current style is checked.
states.meaning: How Aria could write the reply.
states.action: Point at a style to preview it, or choose one.

states.label: Previewing a style
states.behaviour: A sample reply in that style appears beside the list. Nothing changes until they choose it.
states.meaning: What replies would read like.
states.action: Choose it, or look at another.

states.label: Style applied
states.behaviour: The menu closes and the Style chip in the composer reads “Concise”, with × to go back to Normal. One line says where it applies. Their request is untouched.
states.meaning: Replies from now on will be shorter and more direct.
states.action: Send, switch, or go back to Normal.
states.next: Style switched, or Back to Normal

states.label: Style switched
states.trigger: Mid-conversation, they switched Concise to Formal.
states.behaviour: The chip updates and one line says the new style applies from here — earlier replies keep theirs.
states.meaning: The next reply will be formal.

states.label: Back to Normal
states.trigger: They pressed × on the chip (or chose Normal).
states.behaviour: The chip goes; one line confirms Normal, with Undo.
states.meaning: Replies go back to the default style.

states.label: Create a style
states.behaviour: A card above the composer: start from writing they like (paste or upload) or describe the style instead. Generate style is the only AI step; the example is used only to make the style.
states.meaning: Aria can learn how they want replies to read.
states.action: Add an example or a description, then generate.

states.label: Style generated
states.trigger: Aria made a style from their example.
states.behaviour: A name and one line on what it changes, both editable and marked as Aria’s; the instructions behind it, on request; and a preview. Save keeps it in Your styles; Save and use applies it.
states.meaning: Their own style — reviewed before it is used.

simNote: Aria has answered in its Normal style. Open Style, point at a style to preview it, choose Concise and ask again. Then Create & edit styles: Aria makes a style from your own release notes. Switching never rewrites what you typed, and earlier replies keep the style they were written in.
intent: Lets someone set how the agent writes — shorter, more formal, more explanatory, or in their own house voice — without repeating it in every request, and change it at any point in a conversation.
when: When people return to the same kind of reply — summaries, customer emails, explanations for newcomers — and want it to read a consistent way. Not for a single-request instruction, and not for what the agent knows or which model answers.

name: Attachments
oneline: Upload files, photos, docs for the AI to read.

states.label: Nothing attached
states.behaviour: The ordinary composer. Attaching is one control away and it does not go anywhere else — the row appears above the input, inside the same bar.

states.label: Uploading
states.behaviour: The object joins the composer immediately, carrying a determinate bar because there is a real number to show.

states.label: Reading
states.behaviour: Uploaded is not readable. The bar stops claiming a percentage it no longer has, and the word changes.

states.label: Ready
states.behaviour: Name, type, and the word Ready. The composer has grown by exactly one row and nothing else has moved.

states.label: Several
states.behaviour: They wrap within the row. Each keeps its own state, because one failing has nothing to do with the others.

states.label: Too large
states.trigger: The file is over the limit.
states.behaviour: Refused before a byte moves, with the limit in the message, and still listed so it can be swapped rather than hunted for.

states.label: Failed
states.behaviour: A retry control on the object itself, so recovering costs one press rather than finding the file again.

states.label: Image
states.behaviour: A real thumbnail, because for an image it identifies the file faster than the filename does.

simNote: Attach a file from the + in the composer and watch the states it passes through. The one worth reading is the last: removing a file takes it out of what comes next, and cannot unwrite an answer it already shaped.
intent: Temporary context — a file that belongs to this conversation and dies with it.
when: Whenever the material is specific to one question — this contract, this screenshot, this export. It is the right default for anything a person would not want to keep: the cost of attaching is one press and the cost of it being wrong is nothing, because it goes away with the conversation.

name: Connect Data Source
oneline: Sign in to GitHub, Drive, Slack or Notion for live, bounded grounding.

states.label: No sources connected
states.trigger: A fresh agent, before anything has been granted.
states.behaviour: Names the benefit in one line and lists what can be connected as a compact list — not a gallery of logos nobody browses.

states.label: Why access is needed
states.behaviour: Says what the agent cannot reach and why, then what connecting would allow — in the product’s own verbs, before any handoff, and bounded rather than absolute.

states.label: Connecting
states.behaviour: The product does not impersonate the sign-in. It waits, says it is waiting, and leaves a way out.

states.label: Connected
states.behaviour: The word and a dot, in that order, plus a plain statement of what the agent can now reach — bounded, never “all of GitHub.”

states.label: Being used
states.trigger: A request the source can answer arrives.
states.behaviour: A quiet line while the agent draws on the source, settling into a small, checkable receipt — never a progress percentage, because there is no honest one for “reading issues.”

states.label: Several sources
states.behaviour: One surface, grouped by the only thing that decides where a source belongs: connected sources first, each with a switch for whether the agent may draw on it right now, then what can still be added, divided by a single hairline. Neither group is captioned — a switch and a Connect say which half a row is in.
