The switch is availability, not the grant: off keeps the connection and the account, and ending one is a separate, confirmed decision on the connection itself.

states.label: Connection problem
states.trigger: The handoff does not complete, or a sign-in that was working expires or is revoked upstream.
states.behaviour: One state for both, because the product owes the same three things either way: never show it as still connected, say what happened in a sentence a person can act on, and keep the way back to one press. What it must NOT merge is the sentence. A handoff that failed changed nothing and has no account to name; a sign-in that expired was working until it wasn’t, and saying “nothing was changed” to that person is simply false. Same state, same shape, one line and one verb chosen by the cause — which is what the control beside this switches between.

states.label: Manage connection
states.trigger: Manage is pressed on a live connection.
states.behaviour: A compact surface over the connection it manages: the account, what the agent can do with it, reconnect if it needs it, and a way to end it — nothing else.

states.label: Disconnect confirmation
states.behaviour: One press should not be enough to drop a standing grant. The sentence says what changes — new requests only — never a claim about deleting anything already said.

states.label: Disconnected
states.behaviour: Back to the row it started as. Earlier turns that used the source are not rewritten or removed — only new requests lose access.

simNote: Two ways in, and they meet in the same component. Open the composer’s + to go looking for a source, or just send the question and let the agent run into the wall. Afterwards the + is how you add a second source, manage one, or take one away.
intent: An account, not a file — access that outlives the conversation and can be withdrawn.
when: When the answer depends on a live system the person already has an account for, and the access is worth keeping — a tracker, a calendar, a drive, a code host. It is worth offering contextually the first time a request needs it, and worth surfacing in settings afterwards so that what was granted can be re-read months later.

name: MCP Server Connection
oneline: Connect a server, discover what it can do, and decide before the agent uses it.

states.label: Not connected
states.trigger: The agent needs a tool the product does not have.
states.behaviour: One line saying what a server would give it, and one action. Add MCP server opens a name and an address on the same surface — not a settings page, because this happens in the middle of trying to get something done.

states.label: Connecting
states.behaviour: Reaching, validating, discovering — three named steps that resolve one at a time. They fail for different reasons and are fixed in different places, so a spinner cannot do this job. No percentage: nothing here knows one.

states.label: Ready
states.behaviour: Connected is not Ready. Ready is the tool count and the tool list: what the server turned out to offer, grouped by what each one can do, with the schema one press behind the row for whoever wants it.
states.action: Inspect a tool, or let the agent use one

states.label: Needs approval
states.trigger: The agent calls a tool that changes something.
states.behaviour: At call time, with the arguments visible. Allow runs it here and the result settles in place. Always allow is offered on a tool that writes and withheld on one that destroys.

states.label: Tool failed
states.trigger: One call comes back an error.
states.behaviour: The server badge does not move. One tool broke; the other three still work, and the actions are about the call. Retry once and it escalates to the SERVER — which is a different failure with a different fix.
states.action: Retry, and watch the failure change scope

simNote: Ask for something the agent cannot do yet, and watch the connection be built for it — reached, validated, then discovered, which is the step most products skip. Then break one call, and watch the failure change scope from the tool to the connection.
intent: A connection whose capabilities have to be discovered, inspected and approved rather than assumed.
when: Where an agent needs to act in a system through a standard interface rather than a bespoke integration — internal tooling, developer workflows, anything a team runs itself. It is the right pattern when the set of capabilities is genuinely not knowable in advance. It is the wrong pattern when it is: if the integration is fixed and reviewed, use a connector and spare people a capability audit they did not ask for.

name: Knowledge Base
oneline: Persistent, named material the agent can draw on across a project.

states.label: Empty
states.trigger: A project exists and nothing has been trusted to it yet.
states.behaviour: One sentence saying what a source buys that an attachment does not — it outlives the conversation — and one action. Not an empty dashboard: there is nothing to dash.

states.label: Preparing
states.trigger: Sources have been added and cannot be read yet.
states.behaviour: The half of the lifecycle products skip. A file that has finished uploading is not a file the agent can read, and one status for both sends somebody to ask a question thirty seconds too early. One honest word, and no pipeline.
states.action: Wait, or ask from what is already available

states.label: Available
states.trigger: The base is healthy and this project is not using it.
states.behaviour: The resting state products lose. Available is a fact about the base; active is a fact about this project. A base can be available in five projects and in play in one, and only the second changes what an answer is made of.

states.label: Active
states.trigger: The base is in play here.
states.behaviour: Compact: the count, where it applies, a way into the list. Active means the agent MAY draw on it — not that it is doing so, which is the next state and a different fact.
states.action: Open the sources, or ask a question

states.label: Being used
states.trigger: A question arrives that this material can answer.
states.behaviour: Searching, then reading a named number of sources, then the provenance the answer carries. Three moments of one state, because that is how it happens — and no percentage, because nothing in the client knows an honest one.

states.label: Multiple knowledge bases
states.trigger: The project could draw on more than one collection.
states.behaviour: A short list saying which is in play and which merely could be, with the count on every row — because a name alone does not say whether choosing it gives the agent six documents or six hundred. A list, not a dashboard.

states.label: Manage sources
states.trigger: Somebody came to see what is actually in it.
states.behaviour: Every source with its kind, its freshness written for that kind, its own readiness as a word, and its own action. This is the state that has to stay a knowledge base rather than becoming a file manager.
states.action: Remove a source, or add more

states.label: Partially available
states.trigger: One source stopped working and the rest did not.
states.behaviour: "11 available · 1 unavailable" — counted apart, because "12 sources" beside an amber badge reads as twelve broken ones. The base still answers, and Review goes straight to the row that is the reason for the word.
states.action: Review the one that needs a person

states.label: Source unavailable
states.trigger: Sources cannot be read, for two different reasons.
states.behaviour: Two kinds of stop with two different ways out: a file that would not parse offers Retry and Replace; a file you are no longer allowed to open offers Reconnect, because nothing about trying again fixes permission.

states.label: No relevant knowledge
states.trigger: The question falls outside the material.
states.behaviour: It looked and found nothing, and says so. Not an error and not a broken base — the base worked. A base that always has an answer is a base that is inventing them, and this is the state that proves it is not.
states.action: Add sources, or ask without it

states.label: Remove source confirmation
states.trigger: Somebody pressed Remove on one source.
states.behaviour: Names the source, says what the agent will stop doing, and says what is NOT happening — the base and its other eleven sources are untouched. Removing one source and deleting a knowledge base must never read alike.

states.label: Inactive
states.trigger: The base has been switched off here.
states.behaviour: Everything is still in it. Switching a base off, removing it from this project and destroying it are three different acts — one is a primary button, one is reversible in a press, and the third asks again before it happens.
states.action: Use it here again, or delete it

simNote: The project already has a knowledge base, and it was here before this conversation. Ask the question it was built for and watch Active become in use — then ask something it does not cover, break a source, or switch the base off, and see that all three are different things.
intent: Standing context — sources that were here before the conversation and will outlive it.
when: Where the same material informs many conversations — a research corpus, a policy set, a product's own documentation, a team's accumulated notes. The test is lifetime. If somebody would be annoyed to re-upload it tomorrow, it wants to be a knowledge base. If they would be alarmed to find it still there tomorrow, it wants to be an attachment, and the moment a file crosses that line somebody should have agreed to it.

name: Model Selection
oneline: Choose the capability that answers, or let the product choose per request.

states.label: Resting
states.trigger: The product at rest, before anybody has chosen anything.
states.behaviour: One small chip carrying two values: which model, and how hard to think. It is the composer’s own mode slot rather than a control added beside it, and a strong default is already in it — nobody is asked to choose before their first request.

states.label: Picker open
states.behaviour: A list, not a catalogue. Auto sits in its own group above the models because it is a different kind of thing, every row says what it is FOR, and picking one moves the flyout on to the effort screen for that model. The prompt text is untouched throughout.

states.label: Specific model selected
states.behaviour: No router mark: what runs is exactly what the chip says. This is the state Auto must never be mistaken for, because here the person has taken responsibility for the choice.

states.label: Auto selected
states.behaviour: The switch is on, the model list has eased shut, and the chip takes a router mark. Auto says what it weighs — quality and speed — in its own line, on or off, so nobody has to switch it on to find out what it does.

states.label: Model changed
states.trigger: A different option has just been chosen.
states.behaviour: The chip updates and one line says when it starts mattering, in the scope the host actually supports. No toast, no dialog, no success screen — and the conversation is untouched.

states.label: Model unavailable
states.trigger: A model is temporarily out of service.
states.behaviour: Listed, not selectable, and it says what to use in the meantime. Temporary, so it may come back — and no provider error text, because a status code is not a thing anybody can act on.

states.label: Organization restricted
states.trigger: An organisation has narrowed what may be used.
states.behaviour: Reads differently from unavailable on purpose: somebody decided this, and no amount of waiting will change it. The recovery is a person, and it is only offered where the host genuinely has that flow.
states.action: Lose the model you were using

states.label: Fallback required
states.trigger: The model already selected can no longer be used.
states.behaviour: The one state that interrupts, because until it is answered the chip is lying about what will happen next. Both ways out are offered — the router, or the list — and it says what is not affected, because the fear at this moment is the thread.

simNote: The selector is the composer’s own chip — there is no second control. Change the model and watch what the menu promises about the conversation, then let the allowance run out and see what you get instead.
intent: Capability as a deliberate choice — or a router that is honest about what it optimises for.
when: Where models differ in ways a person can act on — speed, depth, what the request costs them — and where the person, not the product, owns the prompt. It belongs in professional and enterprise tools where explicit control is a requirement, and it belongs wherever somebody is choosing to wait longer for a better answer.
whenNot: Where the product owns the prompt. If the prompt has been engineered against one model, letting people change it silently degrades a thing they cannot debug. And where routing is genuinely better than choosing, the honest move is a router that names its objective rather than a picker nobody understands. Note the cautionary history: removing a picker people have bonded to is its own failure — one major product pulled its legacy models and reversed within days.
